alias: Cameras - engine log archive lost, repeated or withheld lines
description: Raised by binary_sensor.camera_log_archive_events, which stays on while a gap, resync or withheld event is younger than 35 days and newer than the last press of input_button.camera_log_archive_acknowledge. Triggers: the sensor turning on, a new last_event_at while it is already on (a second event updates the card), plus a boot trigger and a 6-hourly re-assert, because persistent notifications do not survive a restart and a restored binary never transitions at startup. The card is written only from a payload that carries the counters, so a timeout (attributes {}) or a reload never rewrites it as 'None'. Never auto-dismissed by a good run: an overnight permanent loss must still be on screen in the morning. Dismissing the card acknowledges the events it showed (camera_log_archive_event_dismissed). The GAP marker is a code span: bare, '~camlog~' rendered as strikethrough.

data.message:
Latest: {{ state_attr('sensor.camera_engine_log_archive', 'last_event') }}.
Last 35 days: {{ state_attr('sensor.camera_engine_log_archive', 'gap_count_35d') }} gap(s), {{ state_attr('sensor.camera_engine_log_archive', 'gap_min_35d') }} min not archived; {{ state_attr('sensor.camera_engine_log_archive', 'resync_count_35d') }} resync(s); {{ state_attr('sensor.camera_engine_log_archive', 'withheld_35d') }} withheld line(s).
A GAP is a span the journal no longer held when the archive ran - those minutes exist nowhere (a `#~camlog~ GAP` line marks it in the archive). A RESYNC re-archived a window after the journal cursor could not be verified - lines may repeat, none are missing. A WITHHELD line still looked like an identifier after redaction and was written as <WITHHELD> - the redaction rules need a new pattern.
Dismiss this card to acknowledge these events (the same as pressing "Acknowledge camera log archive events"); a later event raises it again. {{ now().strftime('%b %-d %-I:%M %p') }}.
